 Monitoring
Transferrin  
(Tf or TFN)
The iron bound globulin protein 
that responds to the need for 
iron. Can be calculated from 
TIBC and serum iron; half-life 9 
days. See Chapter 7.
Tf increased with low iron stores, 
and prevents build up of highly 
toxic excess unbound iron in  
circulation. In iron overload states 
Tf levels decrease. Because B6 is 
required for iron to bind to Hgb, B6 
deficiency promotes h Tf from the 
h circulating iron that binds to Tf; 
smaller extravascular pool than  
albumin.
Adult male:  
215-365 mg/dL 
(2.15-3.65 g/L)
Adult female:  
250-380 mg/dL 
(2.50-3.80 g/L)
Newborn:  
130-275 mg/dL  
(1.3-2.75 g/L)
Child: 203-360 mg/dL 
(2.03-3.6 g/L)
